n: VDNKh (Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy)
funding: The complex is owned by the City of Moscow, which received the controlling stake from the federal government after a 2013 decision by President Putin. The Moscow government runs it as a state joint-stock company; under its renewal programme 42 heritage monuments on the site have been restored, with federal bodies and state corporations taking part.
note: The 2.4 million square metre site holds about 400 buildings, 49 of them listed heritage, and Mayor Sobyanin reports more than 30 million visitors a year.

propaganda.summary: Stalin's government opened the All-Union Agricultural Exhibition on 1 August 1939 to showcase collectivisation; scholars call it the main Stalinist propaganda venue. Renamed VDNKh in 1959, it displayed Soviet economic achievement until 1991.

funding: The museum is a public cultural institution with legal personality operating under the Romanian Ministry of Culture by Government Decision 90/2010. It is financed from state budget subsidies channelled through the ministry's budget plus its own revenues; the subsidy was 19,490,552 lei in 2024.
note: It occupies the 32,000 square metre former Palace of the Posts on Calea Victoriei, counted 67,916 paying visitors in 2024, and a restoration costing over 100 million euros financed by a Council of Europe Development Bank loan was announced in October 2024.

propaganda.summary: Ceaușescu pushed the museum open in 1972 over specialists' objections. It increasingly served his personality cult: before 1989 ten rooms held the Homage exhibition of gifts to Nicolae and Elena Ceaușescu.

funding: The museum is a National Institution established by a decision of the Government of the Republic of Macedonia on 31 July 2008 and opened on 8 September 2011. The Skopje 2014 accounts record 2,110,940 euros of public money spent on its building. The museum's own site lists the Ministry of Culture of North Macedonia first among its institutional partners.
note: The government counted more than 200,000 visitors in its first five years; visits are by compulsory guided tour past 109 wax figures and 85 large history paintings.

propaganda.summary: The VMRO-DPMNE government built the museum under its Skopje 2014 programme and opened it on 8 September 2011. Its compulsory guided tour ends with a party co-founder, merging nation, revolutionary movement and governing party.

n: State Museum of the History of the Temurids (Amir Timur Museum)
funding: The museum is a state museum under the Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Uzbekistan. It was built under Cabinet of Ministers Resolution 99 of 14 March 1996 and fully reconstructed under a presidential decree of 5 February 2026.
note: The circular building with a blue cupola modelled on Samarkand's Gur-e-Amir faces the Timur equestrian statue on Timurid Square; President Mirziyoyev reopened it on 9 April 2026 with AI-based interactive exhibits.

propaganda.summary: Karimov's government built the museum for Timur's 660th anniversary in 1996 as a centrepiece of the state Timur cult. It displays the Ideology of National Independence and Karimov portraits; Mirziyoyev reopened it in 2026.

funding: The museum is run by the Tatmadaw, Myanmar's armed forces: the Defence Services Museum and Historical Research Institute sits under the Commander-in-Chief's office. Soldiers control its gates and active-duty units supply its docents.
note: The 603 acre site in Zeyathiri Township has twelve display halls with floor space near 540,000 square feet; civilian visitors are rare and staff often outnumber them.

propaganda.summary: The military government opened the 603 acre museum in March 2012. Run by the Tatmadaw, it presents the armed forces' nationalist ideology, with portraits of Ne Win, Than Shwe and Min Aung Hlaing throughout.

funding: The Ministry of Home Affairs created the museum under Than Shwe's State Peace and Development Council and still pays a skeleton staff. A police major from the ministry's Drug Enforcement Division runs it, and the state maintains its site drugmuseum.gov.mm.
note: Three floors of exhibits stand on a 15.11 acre former cemetery site at the corner of Kyandaw and Hanthawady Roads; visitors are mostly students on free field trips, with 4,000 kyat admission for others.

propaganda.summary: Than Shwe's junta inaugurated the museum on 26 June 2001 to publicise its drug eradication campaign. Exhibits cast drugs as a foreign enemy and quote a general calling human rights and democracy big-nation excuses.
